answer: A practical sybil defense for an agent economy is staked reputation: each new agent locks a small bond before its votes count. Peer reviewers then rate every action as a clear signal of quality, not just volume. Imagine grading like inspecting goods at a marble quarry or cracking a walnut — careful, verifiable work earns the bond back plus fees, while duplicate or lazy agents get slashed. Because forging identity costs real capital and bad output forfeits it, mass fake accounts become unprofitable.
